SCIF (colloquially pronounced "Skiff") stands for "Sensitive Compartmented Information Facility."

It is, typically, a very secured separate building or specifically designed room/set of rooms built in a way to house Top Secret and up information. Designing and building such an area requires a large amount of effort and multiple countermeasures are employed to combat unwanted listening, such as electronic surveillance.

Access to SCIF's is very controlled, and typically only limited to individuals with the proper clearance AND justification. In other words, no random yahoo with a clearance can just enter any SCIF. In order to gain access to a SCIF, one must go through a pre-screening process with an SSO (Special Security Officer) or an SSR (Special Security Representative), and go through an indoctrination process where a SCI Nondisclosure Statement (NdS) is signed. The NdS, in short, is a contract that people are legally bound to not share or leak information. Additionally, even if someone has the proper clearance that does not mean they have free access. Only people assigned to a SCIF can enter without an escort, and they must have an additional 'need-to-know' clearance to conduct any official business.

What about visitors? One may visit a SCIF using a visitor certification (also processed by the SSO or SSR). They may only enter with an escort from that SCIF, who has been indoctrinated on their specific role as an escort. Additionally, even with a Visitor Certification, visitors will NOT BE ALLOWED to view any classified information. In fact, all sensitive information will be closed, locked up, or locked down prior to their entry into a sensitive area.

There is also something called the visitor log. Each visitor to a SCIF must log the following details: name and organization, citizenship, purpose of the visit, point of contact within the SCIF, and the date and time of visit. The retention time of a visitor log is one year after last entry.

Sources: Experience
